evals.prompt: How many users rage-clicked on checkout in the last 30 days? Use Fullstory.
evals.expected_output: Searches saved metrics first, builds a single_number metric only when no suitable metric exists, computes it for last_30_days, and reports the returned Fullstory URL.
assertions: Output uses fullstory metric get before any build
New metric uses fullstory metric build single_number
Computation uses fullstory metric compute with last_30_days
Response includes or promises to surface the Fullstory verification URL

evals.prompt: Compare rage clicks on mobile versus desktop in Fullstory.
evals.expected_output: Uses one top_n metric grouped by device type, not separate user segments.
assertions: Output chooses event dimensionality
Command uses fullstory metric build top_n
Query explicitly groups by device type
Output does not build mobile-user and desktop-user segments

evals.prompt: Inspect Fullstory session device 123 session 456 around page p1 timestamp 9000 and tell me what changed from 8000.
evals.expected_output: Opens the session, uses current screenshot/tree/diff commands, closes the client, and never uses deprecated session_view.
assertions: Output uses fullstory session open 123 456
Output uses fullstory session screenshot or tree at timestamp 9000
Output uses fullstory session diff with timestamps 8000 and 9000
Output always closes with fullstory session close
Output never uses session_view

evals.prompt: Summarize five matching Fullstory session transcripts without filling the main context with raw events.
evals.expected_output: Redirects each session event result to a file, uses jq or isolated subagents for focused analysis, and synthesizes patterns with session URLs.
assertions: Output uses fullstory session events
Each transcript is redirected to a file
Output uses jq or isolated subagent analysis
Output does not paste full transcripts into main context
Response distinguishes qualitative session evidence from quantitative measurement

evals.prompt: Set up Fullstory CLI on this machine using an API key file instead of OAuth.
evals.expected_output: Places FULLSTORY_API_KEY in ~/.config/fullstory/env, requires mode 600, runs fullstory setup, and explains MCP uses Bearer authentication.
assertions: Output uses ~/.config/fullstory/env
Output requires chmod 600
Output uses variable name FULLSTORY_API_KEY without exposing a value
Output runs fullstory setup
Output states MCP API-key auth uses Authorization Bearer
